profile.constituencyprofile_Text: The Singanamala Assembly Constituency was established in 1962 and has undergone multiple administrative reconfigurations over the years. The constituency’s economy is primarily agrarian, with agriculture forming the backbone of livelihood for most residents. Fertile lands and favorable climatic conditions support the cultivation of various crops, playing a vital role in the local economy. In recent years, the area has also witnessed gradual development in infrastructure and renewable energy. Singanamala holds cultural and historical significance, featuring diverse geographical features and potential for economic expansion. Its strategic location near towns like Anantapuramu, Tadipatri, and Guntakal makes it well-suited for trade, transportation, and tourism development.
profile.geography: The Singanamala Assembly Constituency is located in the north part of Ananthapuramu District, Andhra Pradesh. This prominent constituency in the Rayalaseema region encompasses Six mandals.The constituency mainly having Red soils, with Black soils.
profile.populationDesc: According to the 2011 Census, the population of the Singanamala Assembly Constituency stands at 2,92,414 people, comprising 1,48,841 males and 1,43,573 females. The sex ratio is 966 females per 1,000 males, slightly lower than the district average (978) and state average (993). The area includes 72,424 households
profile.administrationDesc: This prominent constituency in the Rayalaseema region encompasses Six mandals: Singanamala, Garladine, Bukkarayasamudram, Narpala, Putlur and Yellanur.
profile.educationHealthcareDesc: The educational infrastructure consists of  231  primary schools, 57  upper primary schools, and 64 high schools, 11 Junior Colleges 1 Engineering College (SRIT),2 Polytechnical Colleges and 1 Central University near Janthulur Village (Bukkarayasamudram), 6 Social Welfare Residential School, 2 Tribal Welfare Residential School, and 4 Backward Classes Welfare Residential School.,1 Government Junior College, 1 Government ITI, and one private polytechnic. Health care :Singanamala includes One Community Health Centres (CHCs), Ten Primary Health Centres (PHCs), around 84 sub-centres, and 4 Ayush dispensaries.
profile.culturalheritageDesc: Singanamala is rich in cultural landmarks, such as the Gugudu Kullaya Swamy Peerla Makan, Sri Gunti Subramaneswara Swamy Temple, Sri Kondameeda Rayudu Swamy Temple, Sri Durganjineya Swamy Temple.

economy_text.economy_Text:
Singanamala’s Economic Vision Plan (2024–2029) projects robust economic growth, with GCDP rising from ₹10,643 crores to ₹24,257.6 crores (CAGR 18%), surpassing the targeted 15% annual growth. 

Agriculture, contributing 65% of GCDP by 2028-29, drives growth through horticulture (54.16% share, ₹12,446.7 crores) and livestock, fueled by irrigation modernization, crop diversification, and agri-processing. 

The industry sector (18.10% share, ₹4,159.61 crores, CAGR 24.5%) accelerates via construction, renewable energy, and MSME-focused industrial parks.

While the services sector (16.90% share, ₹3,883.83 crores, CAGR 14.7%) diversifies through IT, tourism, and financial inclusion. 

Cross-sectoral emphasis on sustainability, infrastructure, and skill development positions Singanamala as a resilient economic hub by 2029, aligning with the 2047 vision.
economy_text.gcdP_Growth_Text: Between 2024–29, Singanamala’s economic momentum will be anchored in horticulture-driven agriculture, MSME-led industrialization with renewable energy, and service sector diversification in banking, logistics, and digital services. The focus will be on irrigation, skill development, industrial parks, renewable energy adoption, and digital-financial inclusion, laying the foundation for long-term transformation towards the Swarna Andhra 2047 vision
